faqSchema.source:
Often you do not, which is why it is usually picked up at a check-up from the wear pattern, or reported by a partner. Morning jaw ache and temple headaches are common indicators.

No. It protects your teeth from the forces involved. Reducing the grinding itself means addressing the underlying contributors, which we will discuss.

You can, but a generic soft guard fits poorly and can increase clenching. A custom splint is made to your teeth with an even bite across it.

It depends on how heavily you grind. Some people wear through one in a couple of years, others get considerably longer. Bring it to your check-ups so we can monitor it.

There is an adjustment period of a week or two. Most people stop noticing it. If it is genuinely uncomfortable, bring it back and we will adjust it rather than leaving you to persevere.

Worn teeth can often be rebuilt, though extensive wear may require crowns or a staged rehabilitation. Protecting what remains comes first, because there is no point restoring teeth that are still being ground down.

fields.label: Main heading
fields.value: Protecting your teeth from your own jaw.

fields.label: Introduction
fields.value: Grinding and clenching — bruxism — mostly happens at night, which is why most people who do it have no idea. It is usually a partner who mentions the noise, or a dentist who notices the wear.

fields.label: Introduction
fields.value: The forces involved are considerable and sustained. Over years, grinding flattens the biting surfaces, chips enamel at the edges of front teeth, cracks fillings, fractures cusps off molars, and can loosen teeth where gum support is already reduced. It is also a common cause of morning jaw ache and headache.

fields.label: Small heading
fields.value: Assessment first

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Dr Meg will look at the pattern of wear, check your jaw joints and muscles, examine existing restorations, and ask about your sleep, stress and any medications. Grinding has several contributing factors — stress, sleep disturbance, some medications, alcohol, caffeine — and the pattern of wear often indicates how long it has been going on.

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: It is worth knowing that a night guard does not stop you grinding. It protects your teeth while you do, which is a different and more achievable goal.

fields.label: Small heading
fields.value: The guard itself

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: A night guard, or occlusal splint, is a custom appliance worn over the upper or lower teeth while you sleep. It is made from a digital scan of your teeth so that it fits closely and the bite meets evenly across it. Even contact matters: a splint that loads a few teeth unevenly can cause more trouble than it prevents.

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Once made, it is fitted and adjusted in your mouth, and reviewed after a few weeks to check how it is settling and how it is wearing.

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Chemist-bought guards are generally soft, poorly fitting, and can encourage more clenching rather than less. They are not equivalent.

fields.label: Small heading
fields.value: Jaw joint discomfort

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Where grinding is accompanied by jaw joint pain, clicking or restricted opening, Dr Meg will assess the joint as part of the appointment. Management may include a splint, advice on habits and jaw exercises, and in some cases diode laser treatment. The evidence for laser in jaw joint discomfort is still developing, and she will be frank about what it can and cannot be expected to do. Some cases warrant referral.

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: Frequently asked questions

fields.label: Button words
fields.value: How do I know if I grind my teeth?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Often you do not, which is why it is usually picked up at a check-up from the wear pattern, or reported by a partner. Morning jaw ache and temple headaches are common indicators.

fields.label: Button words
fields.value: Will a night guard stop me grinding?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: No. It protects your teeth from the forces involved. Reducing the grinding itself means addressing the underlying contributors, which we will discuss.

fields.label: Button words
fields.value: Can I buy one from the chemist instead?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: You can, but a generic soft guard fits poorly and can increase clenching. A custom splint is made to your teeth with an even bite across it.

fields.label: Button words
fields.value: How long does a night guard last?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: It depends on how heavily you grind. Some people wear through one in a couple of years, others get considerably longer. Bring it to your check-ups so we can monitor it.

fields.label: Button words
fields.value: Is it uncomfortable to sleep in?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: There is an adjustment period of a week or two. Most people stop noticing it. If it is genuinely uncomfortable, bring it back and we will adjust it rather than leaving you to persevere.

fields.label: Button words
fields.value: Can grinding damage be repaired?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Worn teeth can often be rebuilt, though extensive wear may require crowns or a staged rehabilitation. Protecting what remains comes first, because there is no point restoring teeth that are still being ground down.
